item.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM 2025: Understanding the Risks of Large Language Models
item.description:
Tags: ["AI Security", "Large Language Models", "Cybersecurity Risks", "Generative AI", "Risk Management"]
Summary:
  • OWASP updated its Top 10 risks for large language models in 2025.
  • The update reflects new insights from real-world AI deployments.
  • MITRE’s Atlas framework also evolves alongside these changes.
  • The update includes feedback from global AI security experts.
  • It highlights emerging security challenges in generative AI systems.

item.title: When AI financial advice goes wrong: ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini failed UK consumers
item.description:
Author: Giskard Team
Date: N/A
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Financial Advice", "Consumer Protection", "Regulation", "Technology Failures"]
Summary:
  • AI tools like ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini gave poor financial advice to UK users.
  • They often provided outdated or incorrect information.
  • UK-specific financial rules were frequently ignored.
  • The article urges stricter regulation and better AI training.
  • Consumers should consult human advisors for important financial decisions.
  • AI has potential but needs improvements for safe use.

item.title: Improving Methodologies for AI Model Evaluations Across Global Languages
item.description:
Author: Lead Authors: Singapore, Japan, United Kingdom; Contributors: Members of the International Network of AI Safety Institutes
Date: N/A
Tags: ["AI Evaluation", "Multilingual AI", "Cybersecurity", "International Collaboration", "AI Safety"]
Summary:
  • Singapore, Japan, and the UK led a global AI evaluation study.
  • They tested AI models across ten different languages.
  • Over 130,000 cybersecurity prompts were used in the tests.
  • The study created 6,000 new multilingual prompts.
  • Results showed language impacts AI model responses.
  • Limitations include grading subjectivity and limited human review.

Summary:
  • International Network participants collaborated on agentic AI evaluations.
  • The third exercise focused on LLM agents and their risks.
